title: A physical model shows that published hyperpolarized xenon-129 MRI task responses exceed what local blood flow can cause, and that current xenon methods need about 1 cm voxels
abstract: A physical model shows that the large brain responses reported with inhaled hyperpolarized xenon-129 MRI cannot come from local blood-flow changes, and that current xenon methods need voxels of about 1 cm to detect brain activity. This matters because these studies and a patent application present xenon MRI as a functional brain method with about 100 times the signal change of BOLD functional MRI. Hyperpolarized xenon is gas whose nuclear spins are aligned by laser light; after one breath it dissolves in blood, enters the brain, and gives a non-renewable MRI signal that increases with cerebral blood flow (CBF). We modelled xenon uptake, transport and spin relaxation, used a brain template with maps of visual and motor cortex, took human xenon signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) from the literature, and simulated the published processing. Model values are medians with 5-95 % ranges over parameter draws; simulations use nominal values. In fully active grey matter, +50 % CBF raises the xenon signal by 50 % (47-53 %). In the published 12.5 mm projection pixels, it gives about 10 % (at most 12 %) at the best motor pixel and 39 % (at most 48 %) at the best visual pixel. The published mean 'percent signal enhancement' was 123 +/- 60 %, against 1.3 % for BOLD, from one task and one rest breath-hold. With no activation, the largest single-pixel ratio among pixels with SNR above 2 was 123 % (64-209 %) in our simulation, and 71-237 % across masks and delay sets. When changes are divided by the mean brain signal, noise gives 49 % (29-79 %), but 1-2 s differences in bolus arrival between breath-holds change the fitted perfusion slope by 7-120 %. A reported 50-100 % whole-cerebrum rise during a 1-back task needs a global change, not local activity. Per unit volume, the published xenon perfusion maps had 65-280 times less SNR than the arterial spin labelling (ASL) images that they were compared with. To detect a strong visual response at z = 5 (a strict statistical threshold) in a best-placed 5 mm voxel, BOLD needs 2.5 min, ASL 13 min, xenon at a physical ceiling with ideal receive coils 18 min, and current xenon practice about 23 h of breath-holds. Main limits: xenon T1 in human grey matter and the regional blood-flow noise per breath-hold are not measured, the published definition of percent enhancement is not stated, and the template anatomy and SNR anchor favour xenon.

display.caption: Signal change for task versus rest, log scale. Blue: physical model (this work), with CBF-driven changes in fully active grey matter, in the best published projection pixels, and over the whole brain for a local task or a global CBF change. Orange: published claims (2017 whole-cerebrum rise during a 1-back task; 2020 mean percent enhancement of 123 +/- 60 % from the patent application). Green: what the published one-task-one-rest processing gives with noise only (median and 5-95 % of 1000 simulations) under three definitions of percent enhancement, and with 1 s random bolus-timing jitter (its lower 5 % limit is below zero and is cut by the log axis). Grey: 3 T BOLD. The dashed line is the largest change that a doubled CBF can cause.

Smallest cubic voxel side that detects a strong visual (left) or hand-motor (right) response at z = 5, against breath-holds per condition. HP-Xe: current practice, best gas dose with current coils, and a first-principles physical ceiling. BOLD and PCASL at 3 T get the same wall-clock time (3 min per breath-hold). Lines are medians of 2000 parameter draws; bands are 5-95 % (shown for current and ceiling HP-Xe); triangles mean no detection in a 40 mm voxel in most draws. BOLD values of 1 mm are the grid floor. The dashed line is the 3.9 mm vascular blur of 3 T gradient-echo BOLD.

Total scan time to detect a strong visual response at z = 5 in a best-placed 10 mm (left) or 5 mm (right) voxel. Median and 5-95 % of 2000 parameter draws. For HP-Xe, circles assume one breath-hold every 3 min and open squares one every 10 min (polarizer output); breath-holds are whole numbers, at least one per condition.
